he will become a son, O god, to accomplish the work of the gods.”

Saying “So be it,” the sun, that mass of radiance, replied:
“I will father an unmarried maiden's son who will be proud of his might,

Whom everyone in the world will address by the name of Karṇa.
By my grace, O Viṣṇu, for brāhmaṇas whose minds are purified,

There will be no object at all in the world that cannot be given by him, O Keśava.
Such power shall I bestow upon him by your command.”

Having thus spoken to the god, the slayer of Dānavas,
to the great-souled Nārāyaṇa, the thousand-rayed sun vanished right there.

When the god who takes up water, the sun, had gone out of sight,
he also spoke thus with a pleased mind to Vṛddhaśravas [Indra]:

“O thousand-eyed one, this man born of blood, by my favor
having become your own portion, must be dispatched by you to the earth at the end of the Dvāpara.

When the fortunate Pāṇḍu takes Pṛthā as his wife,
and also Mādrī, O illustrious one, he will then go to the forest.

While he is dwelling in the forest, a deer will utter a curse upon him;
and having developed detachment because of that, he will go to Śataśṛṅga.

Desiring sons born of his wife's field, he will speak to his wife;
not wishing for this at that time, Kuntī will say to her husband:

‘O king, I do not at all desire the sons of a mortal;
O ruler of men, by the favor of the gods I desire sons.’

Then, O Śakra, when Kuntī asks you, this man must be given by you;
and by my command, O husband of Śacī, act accordingly.”

Then the lord of gods, distressed, spoke this word to Viṣṇu:
“In this past Manvantara, in the twenty-fourth yuga,

Having descended into the Raghu lineage, in the house of Daśaratha,
for the sake of slaying Rāvaṇa and for the peace of the celestials,

While wandering in the forest in the form of Rāma for the sake of Sītā,
my son was killed by you, O Lord, who wished to benefit the son of Sūrya,

Since the lord of monkeys named Vālin [was slain] by you for the sake of Sugrīva.
Tormented by this grief, I will not take this man as my son.”

To the lord of the gods who would not accept, offering another reason,
Hari spoke to Śunāsīra [Indra] regarding the removal of the earth's burden:

“I myself, O lord, will take an incarnation in the mortal realm
for the destruction of the son of Sūrya and for the victory of your son.

I will act as his charioteer, and I will bring about the destruction of the Kuru clan.”
Then Śakra became delighted by those words of Viṣṇu.

Pleased and accepting the man, [he said,] “May your word come true.”
Having thus granted a boon and dispatched him, the imperishable god himself,

Going forth, the lotus-eyed one said again to Brahmā:
“All this three-world, moving and unmoving, was created by you.

The two of us are your helpers in carrying out the work, O Lord.
Having created it yourself, O god, you do not understand how to cause destruction again.

A loathsome deed was done by you desiring to kill Śambhu,
and by your anger a man was created against the god of gods.

For the purification of this sin, perform the supreme expiation;
taking the three fires, O god, offer the Agnihotra.

At a holy place of pilgrimage, or in a [sacred] region, or in a forest, O Grandfather,
perform a sacrifice together with your wife, out of acceptance of our word.

All the gods, the Ādityas, and the Rudras as well, O lord of the world,
will carry out your order, because you are our master.

One fire is the Gārhapatya, the Dakṣiṇāgni is the second,
and the Āhavanīya is the third: arrange them in three altars.

In the circular one worship yourself; then worship me in the bow-shaped one;
and worship the god Hara in the four-cornered one, with the names of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman.

Producing the fires through austerity and attaining supreme prosperity,
after offering oblations for a thousand divine years, you shall pacify the fires.

Nothing more purifying than the Agnihotra is proclaimed here;
by the properly performed Agnihotra, twice-born men on earth become fully purified.

These paths to the world of the gods have been shown by brāhmaṇas;
one fire should always be maintained by the twice-born householder.

Without the fire, householdership is not attained here by a twice-born man.”
Bhīṣma said:
“That archer named Nara who was born from the skull,

Was he born from Mādhava, or by his own past actions,
or was he produced by Rudra, or intentionally [by Brahmā]?

O brāhmaṇa, this Hiraṇyagarbha was born from the cosmic egg and has four faces;
how did that wondrous fifth face of his arise?

In sattva, rajas is not seen, nor is sattva ever seen in rajas;
how did the blessed Brahmā, established in sattva, experience such an excess [of passion],

Through which a foolish-minded man was sent by him to kill Hara?”
Pulastya said:
“Maheśvara and Hari, both of these two abide on the righteous path.

Nothing accomplished or unaccomplished is unknown to those two great-souled ones.
The fifth face of the great-souled Brahmā was pointing upward.

Then Brahmā became bewildered, swollen with rajas;
then, having created this by his splendor, he thought, ‘It was made by me.

There is indeed no god other than me by whom creation was set in motion,
together with the gods and Gandharvas, crowded with beasts, birds, and animals.’

Thus bewildered, Viriñci came to have five faces again.
The eastern face of his was the promoter of the Ṛgveda;

His second face was the promoter of the Yajurveda;
the third of the Sāmaveda, and the fourth was for the purpose of the Atharvan.

With the fifth face whose eyes looked upward, he recited the Vedas
along with their auxiliary limbs, secondary limbs, legendary histories, secret doctrines, and compendia.

All the gods and Asuras did not shine in the splendor of that face of wondrous radiance,
just as lamps do not shine at sunrise.

Even in their own cities, they lived agitated and mindless;
he regarded no one else, and cast down others with his brilliance.

All the gods, terrified, could neither approach, nor look upon,
nor come before the lotus-born supreme master.”
Deeming themselves as if overcome, their splendor destroyed, / they all took counsel for the benefit of themselves and the deities.
"Let us take refuge in Śambhu, deprived of energy by his energy." / The gods said: / "Salutations to you, Lord of all beings! O Maheśvara, salutations, salutations!
You are the womb of the universe, the supreme Brahman, the eternal one of all beings. / You are the foundation of all worlds, the cause, along with Viṣṇu."
Thus being praised by the divine seers, ancestors, and Dānavas, / the invisible one said this: "O gods, ask for what is desired."
The gods said: / "Granting direct vision, grant what is desired, O god! / Showing compassion to us, let a boon also be bestowed.
Whatever great virility, splendor, vigor, and prowess we had, / all that has been swallowed by Brahmā through the splendor of his fifth mouth.
All our splendors have perished; by your grace, O Lord, / act in such a way, O Maheśvara, that they arise again as before."
Then, with a serene countenance and bowed down to by the gods, / he went to where Brahmā was, whose intellect was bewildered by the egotism of rajas.
Praising the Lord of the gods and surrounding him, they entered. / Brahmā, veiled by rajas, did not recognize that Rudra who had arrived.
Delighting the universe with the splendor of tens of millions of suns, / the soul of the universe, the creator of the universe, the bringer of the universe into being was then seen.
Approaching the seated Grandfather and the entire assembly of gods, / Rudra then [spoke] to Brahmā, the highest lord:
"Aha! Your face shines exceedingly with splendor, O god!" / Having spoken thus, the moon-crested one unleashed a boisterous laugh.
With the tip of the nail of his left thumb, / he severed the fifth head of Brahmā, like a man cutting the core of a plantain tree with his fingernails.
And the severed head remained thereafter in Bhava's hand, / like a second moon standing in the midst of the planetary circle.
And Maheśvara danced with the skull held up in his hand, / like Mount Kailāsa with the sun resting on its summit.
When the head was severed, the delighted gods then / praised the Kapardin, the god of gods who has a bull on his banner, with various hymns.
The gods said: / "Salutations constantly to the bearer of the skull, the time-keeper of Mahākāla, / who is endowed with lordly knowledge, the bestower of all shares!
Salutations to him whose play is joy, who consists of all gods! / In the Kali age you are the maker of dissolution; indeed, you are remembered as Mahākāla.
You are the destroyer of the distress of devotees, and therefore you are called the end of sorrow. / You bring auspiciousness swiftly to devotees; therefore you are remembered as Śaṅkara.
Because Brahmā's head was severed, and you bear the skull, / therefore, O god, you are the skull-bearer. Praised now, be gracious to us!"
Thus praised, Śaṅkara, serene in mind, dismissed the gods / to their own abodes, and the Blessed One remained right there, filled with joy.
Having understood Brahmā's intent, and then the birth of the hero, / having removed the head at their word to pacify the anger of the worlds,
placing his hands in reverent gesture on his head and having bowed to him, / he then praised Prajāpati in this way, to know the supreme Brahman, the treasure of splendor,
with the secret teachings of etymological hymns spoken in the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman: / Rudra said: / "O immeasurable one, salutations to you, the Supreme Self of the supreme!
You are the source of marvels, the imperishable treasure of splendors, / you are the state of the universe through victory, the maker of creation, O one of great splendor!
Salutations to you whose face is turned upward, whose self is sattva, whose self is the earth! / Salutations to you who lie on the water, who are born from water, whose abode is the water!
O you whose eyes are like the petals of a blooming lotus, victory, O divine Grandfather! / For previously I, the Lord, was brought forth by you for the sake of creation.
Salutations to you whose food is always the sacrificial oblation, the lord of the limbs of the sacrifice! / O golden-wombed, lotus-wombed, god-wombed Prajāpati!
You are the sacrifice, you are the vaṣaṭ-call, you are the svadhā, O lotus-born one! / Yet by the word of the gods, O Lord, the head was severed by me.
I am overcome by the murder of a brahmin; protect me, O Lord of the universe!" / Thus addressed by the god of gods, Brahmā spoke words.
Brahmā said: / "The divine friend Nārāyaṇa will make you pure. / He, fortunate, worthy of praise by you, is to be worshiped by me, the all-pervading one himself.
Surely you have been meditated upon by that divine Viṣṇu, / through whom devotion arose in you and the inclination arose to praise me.
From the severing of the head, you are the skull-bearer, the founder of the Soma doctrine; / and you shall deliver hundreds of millions of brahmins, O one of great splendor!
One should perform the vow for the murder of a brahmin; there is nothing else. / Cruel sinners who kill brahmins, perpetrators of evil, are not to be spoken to.
Engaged in forbidden actions concerning the sacred fires, they are not to be spoken to in any way. / If seen by them, looking at the sun must be done.
If contact with a limb is made, O Rudra, one should enter the water with one's clothes on. / Thus one attains the purification seen of old by the wise.
You are that killer of a brahmin; undertake the vow for purification. / When the vow has been performed, you will once again attain many boons."
Having spoken thus, Brahmā departed; Rudra did not comprehend it. / Then he himself contemplated Viṣṇu through the course of meditation,
the companion of Lakṣmī, the giver of boons, the eternal god of gods. / Prostrating with all eight limbs, the three-eyed god of gods,
having bowed, praised the bearer of the conch, discus, and mace: / Rudra said: / "The immortal, ancient one beyond the high, Viṣṇu beyond the highest, of endless prowess,
I constantly remember the supreme, choice Puruṣa, the peerless, ancient Nārāyaṇa, / beyond the highest, firstborn, of fierce speed, the foremost among those of profound, deep intellect.
I am bowed to the god Hari, the ruler, the supreme abode beyond the highest, and the higher abode, / the ultimate abode, both transcendent and immanent, the vast Puruṣa, lord of the higher and lower.
I praise Nārāyaṇa of pure nature, who emitted this subtle [universe], both higher and lower; / because of his eternal presence, may the tranquil, primary Puruṣa be my refuge.
Nārāyaṇa free of taint, the ancient, Viṣṇu beyond the highest, the boundless shore, / the primeval, the foremost among the prudent, the lord of the earth intent on fortitude, forbearance, and peace;

I constantly praise the auspicious one of great majesty, with a thousand heads, manifold feet, / endless arms, with the moon and sun as eyes, the perishable and imperishable, who sleeps upon the ocean of milk.

I praise Nārāyaṇa, the supreme Lord beyond, higher than the high, who is unapproachable by the thirty [gods], / abiding in the threefold creation, having the three sacrificial fires as eyes, perceived through the three principles, the dissolution of the three, the three-eyed.
I bow to the immeasurable Nārāyaṇa, who is white in the Kṛta age and red in the Dvāpara, / and black in the Kali age; and I bow to him who emitted the brahmins right from his mouth,

and the kṣatriyas from his two arms, the vaiśyas from his pair of thighs, and likewise the śūdras from the tips of his feet. / I bow to him whose body is the universe, the ancient, beyond the highest, who has crossed over, the immeasurable,
whose form is subtle, whose form is great, whose form is knowledge, who is formless, / the armor of all gods; I bow to the lotus-eyed one,
the thousand-headed Lord of gods, thousand-eyed, of mighty arms, / who stands pervading the universe; I bow to the Supreme Lord,
the refuge, the divine refuge, Viṣṇu, victorious, eternal, / resembling a dark blue cloud; I bow to him who holds the Śārṅga bow in his hand.
Pure, all-pervading, eternal, having the form of space, everlasting, / free from being and non-being—I bow to Hari who pervades all.
And I see nothing here distinct from you, O Acyuta, / and I behold all this, moving and unmoving, made of you.
While that Rudra, the supreme lord, was thus speaking, / when he had uttered this, the eternal one himself, higher than the highest, appeared before his sight.
Discus in hand, seated on Garuḍa, illuminating the mountain like the sun, he arose; / 'Choose a boon,' the eternal one said, 'I have come as a giver of boons, the best for you.'
When this was said, Rudra, best among gods, spoke: 'Lord of the gods, may I attain supreme purity! / Indeed, no other remover of this sin is seen as foremost, except you.'
'Overcome by the murder of a brahmin, my body has turned black, / there is a smell of a corpse on my limbs, and my ornaments are of iron.'
'How may this form of mine not remain so, O Janārdana? / What shall I do, O great god, so that my former body may return?'
'By your grace it will come to be; tell me that, O Acyuta.' / Viṣṇu said: / 'The murder of a brahmin is supreme, terrible, and brings all suffering to the utmost.'
'Even in the mind one should not entertain the contemplation of this sin. / By you, through the god's command, this firm practice has been understood.'
'Now, O mighty-armed one, perform what was spoken by Brahmā: / rub ash over all your limbs three times a day upon your body.'
'Bear bones on your crest, on your ears, and in your hand; / as you do so, O Rudra, there will be no hardship at all.'
Having thus instructed him, that lord, accompanied by Lakṣmī, vanished from that place; / Rudra did not perceive him [go].
Skull in hand, the lord of gods wandered over this earth: / to the Himālaya along with Maināka and together with Meru;
to Kailāsa, to the entire Vindhya, and to the great Nīla mountain; / to Kāñcī, Kāśī, Tāmraliptā, Magadhā, and Āvilā;
to Vatsagulma and Gokarṇa, and likewise to the northern Kurus; / to Bhadrāśva, Ketumāla, and the region of Hiraṇyaka;
to Kāmarūpa, Prabhāsa, and Mount Mahendra; / overcome by the murder of a brahmin, wandering about, he found no refuge.
Filled with shame, constantly looking at the skull stuck in his hand, / shaking his hands repeatedly, distracted again and again,
when, as he shook his hands, the skull did not fall, / the thought then arose in him: 'I will undertake this observance.'
'Along my path the twice-born will go in every direction.' / Having reflected thus for a very long time, the god wandered over the earth.
Reaching Puṣkara, he entered an excellent forest, / filled with various trees and creepers, resounding with cries of diverse beasts,
perfumed by a gentle breeze bearing the fragrance of many tree-blossoms, / the ground adorned with flowers dropped as if intentionally,
rich with diverse fragrances and other savors, with ripe and unripe fruits; / delighted by the fragrance of blossoms, he entered among the groves of trees.
'To me who worship here with devotion, Brahmā will grant a boon; / through Brahmā's grace, the desired knowledge associated with Puṣkara will be attained,'
'which destroys sin, calms evil, and increases nourishment, fortune, and strength.' / As Rudra of immeasurable splendor was thus meditating,
Brahmā, the lotus-born, then arrived, pleased by his devotion; / and the teacher, raising up Rudra who had bowed down, spoke:
'Through the practice of divine observances I have been worshipped by you, / by you with exceeding faith, longing for the sight of me.'
'For humans as well as deities behold me when standing in observance; / according to your desire, I grant you a boon—the most excellent boon.'
'Since this observance has been performed for the fulfillment of all desires / with disposition of mind, speech, and body, and with a satisfied inner self,'
'tell me, what desire of yours shall I grant as you wish?' / Rudra said: / 'This very sight, O Blessed One, is today an ample, great boon,'

since you have been seen, O one worthy of worship by the world, O creator of the world, homage to you,
[achieved] through a great sacrifice to be accomplished and acquired over a long time.
'which expends life itself, you, O god, are seen. / This skull, O lord of gods, has not fallen from my hand, O all-pervading one.'
'Shameful among the ṛṣis is this course of conduct, vile, O all-pervading one; / by your grace, this observance of the skull-bearer has been performed.'
'Let this great vow accomplished for one who has surrendered be declared here: / in which holy region should I cast this away? Tell me!'
'So that I may become purified among the sages of cultivated soul.' / Brahmā said: / 'There is an ancient abode of the Lord, [named] Avimukta.'
'Kapālamocana will be your sacred ford there; / I and you reside there, and Viṣṇu too will be present.'
'Upon seeing you there, even those who have committed great sins / will enjoy pleasures and become purified in my abode.'
'The Varaṇā and the Asī are two rivers dear to the gods; / in the sacred precinct between them, the sin of murder never enters anywhere.'
'Foremost of holy fords is this ford, your foremost of sacred fields; / humans who attend this field until the fall of their body,'
'when dead, go to heaven on a swan-borne vehicle, free from all fear. / A sacred precinct measuring five krośas has been given by me to you.'
'When the Gaṅgā flows through the midst of the sacred field toward the ocean, / then that great, holy city will arise, O Rudra.'
'Holy is the northward-facing Gaṅgā, and eastward-flowing is the Sarasvatī; / for two yojanas the river Jāhnavī flows northward.'
'There indeed all the gods together with Indra, along with me, / having arrived, will take up residence; release the skull there!'
'Those who, having gone to that holy ford, will please the ancestors / with offerings of rice-balls and funeral rites, will have an imperishable world in heaven.'
'A man who has bathed in the great ford at Vārāṇasī is freed / from sin committed in seven births; merely by going there he is liberated.'
'That sacred ford is celebrated as the best of all sacred fords; / living beings who, bowed before you, abandon their vital breaths there,'
'having attained the state of Rudra, rejoice together with you. / Even there, whatever gift is given by a self-controlled person, O Rudra,'
'great will be the fruit of that person whose soul is cultivated. / Those men who perform the purification of body and limbs there,'
'having reached the world of Rudra, rejoice, ever happy. / Worship, muttering of mantras, and burnt-offerings performed there by embodied beings,'
'bring endless reward, [granting] heaven to one possessing devotion to Rudra; / and by the gift of a lamp there, a man will obtain the eye of knowledge.'
'Whoever brands and sets free a young, gentle, handsome bull, free from blemish, / goes to the highest state;'
'together with his ancestors he goes to liberation, there is no doubt of this. / What need is there of saying much? Whatever action is performed by men there'
'with an eye to dharma, that shall bear infinite fruit; / that holy ford is regarded on earth as the cause of heaven and final liberation.'
'It brings endless reward through bathing, recitation, and burnt-offerings; / having gone to the ford of Vārāṇasī, devoted to Rudra with faith,'
'those who have met their death there are devotees, of this there is no doubt; / the ancestors should be known as the Vasus, and the grandfathers as the Rudras.'
'Great-grandfathers are thus the Ādityas'—such is the Vedic revelation. / The threefold rule for the offering of the ball of food has been told by me, O sinless one."
The offering of rice-balls must always be made by mortals who come here, / and the offering of rice-balls should be performed in that very place by their sons with devotion.
Those good sons indeed bring happiness to the ancestors. / I have told you of this pilgrimage place, which grants liberation even by its mere sight.
Having bathed in the water there, one is freed from the bond of rebirth. / Freed from the slaying of a brahmin, O Rudra, stay at your ease
in Avimukta, which I have given [you], together with your wife.” / Rudra said: / “In all the pilgrimage places on earth, I together with Viṣṇu
will remain according to your word; this is the boon I have chosen. / I am the god Mahādeva, always to be worshiped by you.
And I will grant you a boon with a contented inner self; / and to Viṣṇu I will grant boons desired in his mind,
as well as to all the gods and sages of purified mind. / I am the giver, I am to be petitioned; no other is to be conceived in any way.”
Brahmā said: / “I will do so, O Rudra, as the auspicious word spoken by you [declares]; / and Nārāyaṇa will fulfill all your words, there is no doubt.”
Having dismissed Rudra in this manner, Brahmā then vanished. / Having gone to Vārāṇasī, Mahādeva established the pilgrimage place.
